div.p: Sir,—lf we awt to remember Michelstown, let us not forget Peterloo ; the anniversary is in the 16th August, and this is the seventieth. The present generation, with very few °attentions, know nothing of the Peterlito Massacre. Political history does not ,11,1 to hen popular study, and Tories would willingly have as forget events like these. They are not subjects likely to he IIiSIOISSeII in Conservative Clubs. div.head: SHIP CANAL.
div.p: _ Steady pnigress continues to be made on this section. In the nver the inner wall of the canal is being extended ' towards 011 Quay Docks, and another copper darn is in ' course of construction. Are . menciment has been made with the work of excavating the rock On the Wid. foreehore, operations now taking place on the bridge side of the Ferry Slip. In consequence of the building of the wall, and;these operations, the flats have MUCII less sailing room than formerly, and difficulty is some- timea experienced in getting under Runcorn Bridge. On Thursday afternoon a strong headwind was blowing, and the flats had to make numerou.s tacks before they suceentot in passing under the bridge, The romingten and the Bee Came into collision, the bowsprit of the former tearing through the latter's forestial, and the hullo of both boats were damaged ; and the captains pot their respective craft bark into dock to ascertain the extent of the injuries. Railway metals have been laid up to Messrs. Wigan works, and a locomotive is retained to conduct the traffic, far which purpotea large number of waggons have been specially made, TIIE LOSERS PROVIDE A DINNER. A cricket match boween the Ship Canal (No. 6 District Club) and a Workmen's team took place on Saturday, at Morrisbrook,and :kilter a pleasant game ended in victory for the club, the losing train to entertain the winners at dinner. The dinner took Place in the evening, at the old Cheshire Cheese, whim a capital repast wag provided by Host Ireland, which was partaken of by about 30 members and friends. The chair was ably fillol by the • Vice-Captain of the dub, Mr. F. Smith, who was suprios , ted by Mr. ft Browning. lion. see., and several members of the workmen's team. tin the cloth being removed • and the tonal toasts bring given, songs were ably ran- , demi by :Wears. Perteack, Watson, Smith, Browning„ ; and others. A vote of thanks accorded to the host terminated a most enjoyable evening.
